candidates.why_relevant: Hungary's mandatory e-procurement platform; state-owned and public-sector merchants (utilities, toll operator, transport, hospitals) run their card-acceptance / VPOS / POS terminal / payment-gateway tenders here. Free-text search on payments terms surfaces acquirer and PSP contracts and their awarded bidders.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyword crawl of the public procedure list + the publikus API paths (/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-eljaras-nyilvantartas/...) using HU keywords: bankkártya-elfogadás, kártyaelfogadói szolgáltatás, VPOS, POS terminál, fizetési szolgáltatás, online fizetés
candidates.discovered_via_method: HU-language procurement search + snowball to an actual VPOS tender document

negative_findings.description: No public, Hungary-specific list of Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirers or scheme-certified terminal vendors was found. Scheme licensing/certification lists appear to be issued to members, not published per country.
negative_findings.result_summary: EN searches returned only generic scheme PayFac/acquirer model documents and third-party explainers; no HU acquirer roster.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The acquirer/certification universe for HU must be reconstructed indirectly from MNB registers, acquirer ÁSZF documents and trade press rather than from a scheme list.

negative_findings.description: No official public directory of qvik-accepting merchants or of all qvik technical/sub-aggregator providers was located; reporting indicates only a small set of sub-aggregators (OTP Mobil, Raiffeisen mentioned in trade press) but no maintained scheme list surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: HU searches on qvik szolgáltató lista / elfogadóhelyek returned bank product pages and media, not a registry.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: qvik ecosystem participant tracking will need press + provider-site monitoring, with MNB/GIRO pages checked for an eventual official participant list.

negative_findings.description: General web search does not index EKR procedure content or Közbeszerzési Értesítő notice bodies well; payments-specific HU tenders could not be enumerated from search engines alone.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries returned portal landing pages plus one incidental VPOS tender PDF hosted by the contracting authority.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A2 payments tender coverage must run against EKR/KÉ/TED search interfaces and APIs directly; search-engine-based discovery will systematically under-report.

negative_findings.description: Private-sector merchant acquiring RFPs (retail chains, telcos, e-commerce) are not published anywhere public; only the outcome surfaces, usually as a vendor press release.
negative_findings.result_summary: No HU or EN query produced a public private-sector acquiring RFP.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Most acquiring volume changes hands outside public procurement, so award-notice monitoring alone will miss the majority of the market.

coverage_gaps.description: EKR and Közbeszerzési Értesítő were identified but their internal search interfaces/APIs were not exercised with the payments keyword set, so no concrete notice inventory exists yet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated collection pass against EKR public API and KÉ search with the HU keyword list (bankkártya-elfogadás, kártyaelfogadói szolgáltatás, VPOS, POS terminál, fizetési szolgáltatás, azonnali fizetés, qvik) and the payments CPV families on TED.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank acquirers beyond OTP/K&H/MBH/Takarékbank (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB, Gránit) and independent ISOs/ATM-POS operators were not individually scouted in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate all HU acquirers from MNB Intézménykereső, then scout each one's kereskedői elfogadás ÁSZF/hirdetmény page as a monitored source.

coverage_gaps.description: Company-register and contract-transparency sources (e-cegjegyzek/Opten/Bisnode, and central contract-publication obligations under Info tv. §1 melléklet) were not scouted; these can reveal payment-service contracts of state bodies not routed through EKR.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout HU contract-transparency and company-register sources in a follow-up cell pass, in Hungarian.

coverage_gaps.description: Scheme certification / partner listings (Visa, Mastercard, and terminal vendors such as Ingenico, PAX, Verifone HU partner lists) remain unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted pass on vendor partner-locator pages and scheme certification programme pages, in EN, checking whether HU filtering is possible.

brief: Hungary's payments-procurement intelligence rests on three official backbones — EKR, the Közbeszerzési Értesítő and TED — which carry public-sector VPOS/POS/acquiring tenders and award notices (a live 2025 VPOS tender by the national toll operator confirms the pattern), plus MNB's PSD2 TPP data and Intézménykereső as the authoritative actor registers. The qvik/AFR layer is scheme-driven rather than tender-driven: MNB's qvik hub and GIRO Zrt. set the rules, while SimplePay/OTP Mobil, Barion and a small set of sub-aggregators announce integrations and merchant wins on their own sites and in FinTechZone before any registry reflects them. Two structural blind spots dominate: there is no public HU acquirer/scheme-certification roster and no public qvik participant directory, and private merchant acquiring RFPs never surface until a vendor press release. Collection should therefore combine API-level procurement monitoring with diffing of acquirer ÁSZF documents, provider developer docs and HU trade-press feeds.
